exposure: Newborns who did not receive infant formula
prenatal care in public and private service
prenatal care in a private service
cohort: 14,531 postpartum women and newborns referred to rooming-in in Brazilian hospitals
finding: Several factors were associated with infant formula supplementation, including cesarean delivery and non-breastfeeding in the delivery room, while factors like teenage age, lower maternal education, and lower economic class reduced the probability.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of infant formula supplementation (OR = 1.83; 95% CI: 1.41-2.38).
birth_weight: Prematurity (<2.5 kg) and high birth weight (≥4 kg) were associated with infant formula supplementation
